archimate:Principle.name: orchestration
archimate:Principle.documentation:
CONTEXT
The Integration Layer Pilot proves three patterns on Azure Integration Services. For Orchestration, a consuming application calls a REST API through API Management, and the API returns data from the source system. The pilot uses a new read-only MOP API v1, hosted on AKS and secured with Entra ID OAuth 2.0, as the Orchestration Service described in the Integration Layer low-level design (v0.11). This also proves that a new API can be built to the HLD standards, including the DSA and GEMINI header tags, the canonical model and the standard error format.
The API is being built against a copy of the MOP Oracle database on an Azure VM. That copy works for pilot implementation only. The API cannot move to non-production or production.
The live MOP database is on-premise, on Windows Server 2008 R2 behind an end-of-life firewall. It is linked to PCS, L&C and TMS through Oracle database links, and PCS depends on Oracle Forms 11g and Windows 2008. The firewall owner will not change the firewall, because a fault could take PCS down. Rebuilding the database links on their own was ruled out, because of the circular references between systems. An earlier Oracle 11g to 19c migration produced the Azure VM copy, but it has stalled and the reason is not yet confirmed.
At the 11 November MOP database meeting, the team decided against Azure Relay, because it adds a new dependency on legacy infrastructure. The meeting concluded that MOP cannot be moved on its own and that a permanent fix does not fit in the pilot timeframe. No decision was made on an alternative, and the options are to be set out for a decision on the pilot route.
PROPOSAL
Use Option 2 for the pilot: a copy snapshot of the MOP database copied to Azure, with MOP API v1 reading from the copy as a temporary, read-only source.
The API will take its data source from configuration, so the copy can be replaced by a permanent source later without changing the API or its consumers. The snapshot is a temporary measure and is not the target state.
How it would work - A snapshot copy the MOP data from the on-premise database to the Azure Oracle copy, reusing existing database copy jobs where possible. - MOP API v1 stays read-only and reads only from the Azure copy. - No new inbound connection is made to the on-premise database, and the end-of-life firewall is not changed. - PCS, L&C and TMS are not touched.
Why this option - It is the quickest route and read-only access fits the pilot use case. - It adds no risk to PCS, L&C or TMS and does not rely on the end-of-life firewall. - A permanent fix (migrating or decoupling MOP) does not fit in the pilot timeframe. - A configurable data source keeps the integration layer independent of where the data comes from.
Options reviewed: - Option 1(REJECTED), Azure Relay to the on-premise database: rejected, as it depends on the end-of-life firewall and adds risk to PCS. - Option 3(DEFERRED), migrate MOP with PCS, efin and TMS: long-term, beyond the pilot timeframe. - Option 4(DEFERRED), decouple MOP from PCS, and TMS: long-term, a separate exercise. - Option 5(OPEN), use a different system for the pilot: open, to be confirmed. - Option 6(REJECTED), database mirroring: has techical limitation that might impact existing applications using the data.
Consequences - Data is not up to date, so consumers cannot rely on real-time values. - It adds a copy to the estate, which some stakeholders see as against the aim of simplifying it, so it must be documented as temporary with an agreed exit. - The Azure copy needs an owner, support, and a refresh process with monitoring.
Conditions and open points - Confirm whether the PCS schema is in the Azure copy. - Confirm whether existing copy jobs can be reused. - Confirm the status of the 11g to 19c migration work. - Agree the data classification and access controls for the copy. - Agree the exit criteria for replacing the snapshot.
Status: Proposed. A decision from the MOP and architecture owners is pending.
